title: The Self-Checkout (Chas McIvor)
style: jazz lounge piano bar dry wit spoken word observational 104bpm upright bass brushed snare deadpan baritone male vocal life philosophy absurdist supermarket
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
The self-checkout machine was designed by an optimist
Who thought we all wanted to become a checkout analyst
Unexpected item in the bagging area — I know
That item is my shopping and I put it there — let's go

[Pre-Chorus]
I have a loyalty card — it doesn't make me loyal
It makes me stand there with my phone while things begin to boil

[Chorus]
The self-checkout knows something I don't know
It knows that half of human dignity is putting on a show
The self-checkout has me scanning and guessing the weight of fruit
I'm the customer but I'm also the checkout — that's the absolute
That's my boy

[Verse 2]
There's always a supervisor who stands just close enough to watch
Without actually helping with the thing that's gone to botch
She has a master key that unlocks all my problems
But she's waiting for me to fail before she solves them

[Bridge]
I went in for one thing and I came out with a crisis
A trolley full of items and a set of minor prices
The self-checkout said "thank you for shopping with us today"
In a voice that suggested I should maybe go away

[Outro]
Self-checkout knows… unexpected item… self-checkout knows
That's my boy
